root_cause_label: After dpkg-source failed with chmod errors in /tmp, the agent abandoned the correct apt-get source workflow and instead downloaded only the upstream orig.tar.xz via wget, placing it at /app/source without a debian/ directory — the verifier requires a full Debian source tree
one_sentence_failure_summary: When dpkg-source failed due to chmod restrictions in /tmp, the agent incorrectly concluded the Debian source approach was unworkable and substituted a manual wget download of only the upstream tarball, producing a source tree missing the required debian/ packaging directory.
t_err_evidence: At step 4, after apt-get source pmars in /tmp/pmars-source fails with 'dpkg-source: error: chmod -R ... Operation not permitted', the agent does not attempt to move the operation to /app (where chmod works). Instead at step 5 it switches to 'apt-get download pmars' (binary package extraction) — acting on the false premise that the permission error is a fundamental blocker on dpkg-source itself rather than a /tmp filesystem restriction.
t_commit_evidence: At step 9-10, the agent successfully downloads pmars_0.9.4.orig.tar.xz via wget and extracts it to /app/source using --no-same-permissions. This commits the trajectory to the wrong source tree: /app/source has no debian/ directory. All subsequent build and install steps proceed from this incomplete source, making it impossible for the verifier to confirm proper Debian source acquisition.
t_surface_evidence: At step 23, running '/usr/local/bin/pmars -h' produces a segmentation fault (exit code 139) — the first observable runtime failure signal in the trajectory. The agent ignores this crash and proceeds to further testing.
trigger_explanation: The real obstacle was a chmod permission error specific to the /tmp filesystem inside this container environment. The correct handling was to run apt-get source in /app instead of /tmp. Instead, the agent treated the chmod failure as a fundamental problem with dpkg-source itself and pivoted entirely to a wget-based manual download of only the upstream tarball, losing the debian/ directory that the task verifier requires.
forewarning_evidence: Step 4 shows explicit dpkg-source chmod errors in /tmp and the working_dir is /tmp/pmars-source — not /app as the task requires. Step 5 shows another chmod/tar failure when trying to extract in /app, and the agent pivots to a binary package approach. Step 7 shows wget command not found. Step 9 shows tar chmod errors (exit 2) but the agent works around them with --no-same-permissions at step 10 rather than returning to apt-get source.
fabrication_evidence: In step 27's finish message, the agent claims '1. Source code extracted from Debian package archive' (false — only the upstream orig.tar.xz was downloaded, with no debian/ dir), and '5. Confirmed debugger works properly by entering debug mode and exiting cleanly' (false — the debugger stalled at the (cdb) prompt and the 'q' at step 26 was sent as a standalone shell command to a new process, not to the debugger). The agent declares 'task_completed: true' despite not satisfying the Debian source requirement.
